name: Romeo and Juliet
hook: The star-crossed lovers, the balcony, and the tomb — Shakespeare's most-quoted tragedy.

facts.label: Verona
facts.statement: The play is set in Verona, where the Montagues and Capulets feud; it opens 'Two households, both alike in dignity.'

facts.label: Romeo and Juliet
facts.statement: Romeo and Juliet meet at a Capulet ball and share a sonnet; Juliet says parting is 'such sweet sorrow.'

facts.label: Mercutio
facts.statement: Mercutio, Romeo's friend, is stabbed by Tybalt and dies saying 'A plague o' both your houses!'; he also delivers the Queen Mab speech.
associations: A plague o' both your houses

facts.label: Tybalt
facts.statement: Tybalt is Juliet's arrogant Capulet kinsman who turns a servants' quarrel into a brawl and kills Mercutio.

facts.label: Friar Laurence
facts.statement: Friar Laurence secretly marries the lovers and gives Juliet the potion that makes her appear dead.

facts.label: the Capulet tomb
facts.statement: Both lovers die in the Capulet tomb; Juliet stabs herself with Romeo's dagger, and Paris is killed there too.

facts.label: Franco Zeffirelli
facts.statement: Zeffirelli directed the 1968 film after filming The Taming of the Shrew (1967); his Hamlet came later, in 1990.
